page_decision:
BUILD A NEW DEDICATED SIBLING PAGE (route key `cite`), built with the shared-component pattern of the existing `ApiDocs.astro` — NOT by extending `embed-badge`, NOT by consolidating with redirects.

Why new page (all three planners agree, and I concur): (a) distinct search/answer intent — `embed-badge` = "get a widget/img for my site" (webmaster); cite page = "how do I attribute/reference this data" (press, researcher, teacher, blogger). Merging blurs both pages' topical focus. (b) Zero equity risk: `embed-badge` is already indexed, footer-linked and internally linked from every country page; a new URL is purely additive. (c) No redirects needed — today's "Cite this data" is an in-page H3 inside AuthorityLinks.astro with NO URL of its own, so there is nothing to 301. (d) It upgrades the 260623-wd6 citation-seeding function: a canonical "how to cite / link us" hub with copy-paste HTML/Markdown/plain attribution is exactly the surface that generates external backlinks — directly serving the domain-authority bottleneck in project memory.

DECISIVE ARCHITECTURE CALL (diverges from all 3 planners): implement as ONE shared `src/components/CitePage.astro` (prop: `lang`) that holds all markup, an inline per-language `copy: Record<Lang, {...}>` object, the JSON-LD call, and the single client `<script>` — imported by 7 four-line page files at the localized slug dirs. This mirrors the repo's OWN newest precedent (`ApiDocs.astro` + 7 thin `api/index.astro` files, and `RegionsIndex`), whose code comment explicitly says copy is inlined "to avoid threading ~30 more keys through the large i18n/ui.ts table." The planners variously proposed adding ~35 `cite.*` t() keys to ui.ts (planners 1 & 2) — I reject that: ui.ts is already ~3,700 lines, and a shared component reads its copy exactly once, so there is no duplication argument for the ui.ts round-trip. Only ONE ui.ts change is required: the `cite` slug in the `routes` map (×7), which is mandatory because hreflang (Base.astro) and the sitemap (astro.config.mjs serialize) both derive alternates from it. Reusable existing keys (`nav.home`, `badge.copy`, `badge.copied`, `badge.select_country`, `badge.preview`) are pulled via `useTranslations` — no new translations for those.

Effort: Medium. No changes to Base.astro, astro.config.mjs, or utils.ts. One new seo.ts helper, one shared component, 7 thin pages, 1 routes key ×7, AuthorityLinks edit, 1 Footer link.
final_page_spec: Shared component `src/components/CitePage.astro` (props: `{ lang: Lang }`). Uses `loadLatestScores()` sorted by localized name (like embed-badge/ApiDocs), `getLastmodMap().snapshotDate` for the SSR access-date fallback, `useTranslations(lang)` for reused keys, and an inline `copy: Record` map for all cite-specific strings. Wrapped in `` (Base auto-emits canonical + 7 hreflang + x-default + Footer). SECTIONS IN ORDER: 1. Breadcrumb (reuse Breadcrumb.astro): Home (`t('nav.home')`, `/${lang}/`) → {copy.title}. Also emitted as BreadcrumbList in JSON-LD. 2. HEADER: H1 = copy.title; lede = copy.intro (names the audiences + "pick a country or the whole dataset, then copy a ready-made citation"). Static, AI-citable prose. 3. WHAT YOU'RE CITING (H2 = copy.whatHeading, body = copy.whatText): declares the citable Dataset identity — daily-updated scores for 240+ countries, 40+ public sources, CC BY-NC 4.0, "because it updates daily, always cite your access date." Inline links to methodology, sources, and API (`/${lang}/${r.api}/`). Human mirror of the Dataset JSON-LD node; anchors E-E-A-T. 4. CONTROL BAR (the single live-preview driver): label reuses `t('badge.select_country')`; `

TITLES (copy.title; Base renders it — keep ≤~40 chars): en "How to Cite This Data", it "Come Citare Questi Dati", es "Cómo Citar Estos Datos", fr "Comment Citer Ces Données", pt "Como Citar Estes Dados", zh "如何引用此数据", de "Diese Daten zitieren".
DESCRIPTIONS (copy.description, unique per lang, ≤160 chars, keyword-bearing): en "Cite or link IsItSafeToTravel's daily travel-safety scores for 240+ countries. Ready-made attribution in plain text, HTML, Markdown, APA, MLA and BibTeX. Free, CC BY-NC 4.0." (localize the same shape for the other 6).

JSON-LD: add ONE builder to src/lib/seo.ts (keeps seo.ts the single JSON-LD source per CLAUDE.md): `buildCitePageJsonLd(title, description, canonicalUrl, lang, breadcrumbItems, faqItems)` returning `{'@context':'https://schema.org','@graph':[ WebPage, Dataset, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList ]}` where inner nodes carry NO own @context. WebPage = {@type,@id:canonicalUrl,url,name:title,description,inLanguage:localeMap[lang]}. Dataset = REUSE `buildDatasetJsonLd()` (already returns a node without @context; carries CC BY-NC license + DataDownload→scores.json + measurementTechnique; its description is ~140 chars so it satisfies Google's Dataset 50–5000 length rule). FAQPage = {@type:'FAQPage',mainEntity:[…]} built from faqItems. BreadcrumbList = itemListElement from breadcrumbItems (build inline, no @context). VERDICT: OMIT HowTo (Google deprecated HowTo rich results in 2023 — no benefit, only bloat). This graph is the correct lean set that AI answer engines parse for a "how to cite this dataset" page.

HREFLANG + SITEMAP: fully automatic, ZERO astro.config.mjs / Base.astro changes. Base builds hreflang from getAlternateLinks(pathname)→getLocalizedPath (translates the slug segment via routes[lang]); serialize() rebuilds item.links from the same functions and the chunked sitemap auto-includes each prerendered /{lang}/{slug}/. REQUIREMENTS: (1) all 7 `cite` slugs present in routes; (2) all 7 page files exist. If a slug key is missing in one lang, getLocalizedPath silently passes the segment through untranslated → broken cross-lang hreflang for the cite page (and validate-seo will NOT catch it — see below). So all 7 are mandatory and must be added in the same commit.

REDIRECTS: none.

INTERNAL LINKING (net strictly ≥ today): (a) NEW site-wide Footer link on all ~1,892 pages → strong internal PageRank to the new URL; (b) country-page contextual link in AuthorityLinks.astro, deep-linked `/${lang}/${r.cite}/#c=${iso3}` (per-country seeding preserved, pre-scoped); (c) reciprocal cite⇄embed-badge and cite→api/methodology/sources/legal links forming a "Data & attribution" cluster.

VALIDATE-SEO IMPACT: stays all-pass (2213). The gate samples ONLY homepages + en/country/* (+ JPN dataset + advisories + llms-full); it never enumerates the cite page, so the new page adds no checks and cannot fail the gate, and the AuthorityLinks edit touches no JSON-LD/meta/country @graph. CAVEAT: because the cite page is unchecked, hreflang/slug correctness is on the executor — after `npx astro build`, manually grep the 7 dist/client/*/…/index.html for `rel="alternate"` completeness before commit.

rejected_ideas:
EXTEND embed-badge in place (rejected by all 3, I concur): it targets a different intent (visual widget vs textual/academic attribution), is already indexed/footer-linked/country-linked, and would force an H1/title/keyword compromise plus 7 localized 301s if renamed — high blast radius for a UX request, and it buries the badge tool webmasters already find.

CONSOLIDATE-with-redirects (rejected): moot — today's 'Cite this data' is an in-page H3 with NO URL, so there is nothing to 301; a new URL is purely additive.

Adding ~35 cite.* t() keys to ui.ts (proposed by planners 1 & 2 — REJECTED): the repo's own newest convention for a shared utility page (ApiDocs.astro, RegionsIndex) is an inline per-language copy map inside the component, with an explicit code comment that this avoids threading ~30 keys through the 3,700-line ui.ts. A shared component reads its copy once, so there is no duplication cost. Only the `cite` routes key must live in ui.ts. This is the single biggest maintainability win and it resolves the planners' main disagreement.

Localizing APA/MLA/BibTeX wording per language (REJECTED): academic citation styles are English-language standards and the dataset name is the English 'IsItSafeToTravel'; keeping those three templates identical across all 7 langs (only {name}/{url}/{date} vary) removes ~18 fragile hand-translations with no correctness loss. Only plain/HTML/Markdown connectives ('accessed'/'consultato'/...) are localized.

Query-param deep link `?c=iso3` (planners 2 & 3 — REJECTED in favor of hash `#c=iso3`): hash is purely client-side and never creates a crawlable param-URL variant, giving zero SEO surface. Canonical is pathname-only either way, so both are safe, but hash is strictly cleaner.

Chicago format and a HowTo JSON-LD node (proposed by planner 1 — DROPPED): APA+MLA+BibTeX already cover academia; Chicago is marginal maintenance. Google deprecated HowTo rich results in 2023, so a HowTo node yields no rich result and only bloats the graph.

Full removal of the AuthorityLinks `canonicalUrl` prop + editing 7 country [slug].astro call sites (proposed by planners 2 & 3 — DEFERRED): astro build does not typecheck, so an unused prop is harmless; leaving it avoids touching 7 hot country templates. Optional later cleanup.
risks_and_safeguards:
CITATION-SEEDING REGRESSION (constraint #4): removing the country-page <code> attribution line could reduce external-link seeding. SAFEGUARD: the function becomes MORE discoverable — a site-wide Footer link (all ~1,892 pages) + a contextual AuthorityLinks link on every country page deep-linked `#c=iso3` (per-country, pre-scoped) + a destination that now offers 6 copy-paste formats (incl. a real HTML `<a>` backlink and Markdown) instead of one. Net strictly ≥ today.

VALIDATE-SEO BLIND SPOT: the gate samples only homepages + en/country/* (+ JPN dataset/advisories/llms-full), so it neither asserts nor protects the new cite page. A missing slug in one routes[lang] or a folder/slug mismatch silently ships broken cross-lang hreflang. SAFEGUARD: Task 1 adds all 7 slugs in one commit; Task 9 greps the 7 built files for full rel=alternate + self-canonical before push. The 2213 checks stay green (country @graph and meta untouched).

BIBTEX / HTML ESCAPING: backslashes and braces inside Astro + JS template literals are a known footgun (\\url, doubled braces, angle brackets). SAFEGUARD: Task 3/9 verify the rendered textarea output byte-for-byte for BibTeX and the HTML badge snippet in en + one accented locale (e.g. Côte d'Ivoire) so SSR and JS-regenerated values match.

LICENSE (NC) MISUSE: CC BY-NC 4.0 means commercial press/bloggers legally cannot reuse. SAFEGUARD: whatText + FAQ Q1 + License section state this up front and route commercial requests to seek separate permission (there is no commercial license today — see open questions).

ACCESS-DATE CORRECTNESS: academics rely on it; a build-time date would be wrong for a static page. SAFEGUARD: date is client-computed (toISOString ISO yyyy-mm-dd); SSR fallback uses the snapshot date so no-JS/crawler output is still a valid citation; accessedNote explains the auto-update.

DEEP-LINK GUARD: `#c=` may reference an iso3 not in the select (sparse territory). SAFEGUARD: JS falls back to the default first-country selection silently.

ROLLBACK: fully additive and isolated — revert the AuthorityLinks + Footer hunks, delete CitePage.astro + 7 page files + the seo.ts helper + the 7 routes entries. No shared infra (Base.astro, astro.config.mjs, utils.ts) is modified, so a single-commit revert is clean.
open_questions: Commercial-license messaging: the page (whatText + FAQ Q1 + License section) will state that CC BY-NC 4.0 forbids commercial reuse and that 'commercial use requires separate permission.' There is no commercial license or dedicated contact today — is it acceptable to route such requests to the existing Feedback page, or does the owner want different wording (e.g. omit the commercial-permission sentence entirely)? This is the one decision that is genuinely the owner's; everything else is specified.
